applicableAreas: Site perimeter boundaries
valley view road frontage
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 4, 9, 21 for existing overhead facilities. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows existing overhead electric lines (OHE) and power poles along the perimeter, and there is a transformer on pad shown outside the property near Valley View Road. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows existing OHE lines on site edges with dashed line notation. However, the vision analysis of Sheet 21 reveals these are labeled as 'OHE' but specifics are limited: no callouts identify all three-phase conductors, neutral conductor, or transmission lines explicitly. Guy wires are noted on Sheet 4 legend but unclear if shown for existing poles on this specific site.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires all existing electric facilities to be shown, including 'poles, all three-phase conductors, neutral conductor, transmission lines, towers.' While existing overhead lines are depicted on Sheets 4 and 21, the plans do not provide explicit callouts or labels identifying: (1) all three phase conductors, (2) neutral conductor specifically, (3) transmission line voltage designation, or (4) detailed pole heights and cross-arm dimensions. The vision analysis found OHE lines but noted no detailed pole cross-sections or conductor specifications. This falls short of the 'completely shown' requirement in the deficiency title.
findings.comment: Existing overhead electric facilities are partially shown but not completely. Please add detailed callouts to identify all three-phase conductors, neutral conductor, transmission voltage designations, and poles with cross-arm details and heights to all sheets showing existing overhead facilities.

applicableAreas: All elevation/profile views with existing overhead facilities in proximity
findings.observation: Examined available section and elevation sheets. Sheet 21 references 'See Sheet 19 for Profile' but vision analysis of Sheet 19 found NO profile views present—only plan view with notes. No dedicated section views showing heights, conductor spacing, or clearance envelopes were located on Sheet 19. No profile sheets explicitly showing existing electrical pole heights and all conductors were found in the available plan set. While Sheet 3 contains transmission clearance notes, no graphical cross-sections or elevation views demonstrating pole heights and clearance envelopes are present.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires section views to show 'height of existing electrical poles and all conductors with clearance envelopes.' Although section views exist in the plan set (e.g., storm sewer profiles on other sheets), the electrical profile information referenced on Sheet 21 is not provided. The absence of dedicated electrical section views with pole heights, conductor elevations, and clearance envelopes (typically 7.5 feet horizontal minimum clearance per UCM § 1.10.3) means the clearance compliance cannot be verified graphically.
findings.comment: Section views showing existing electrical pole heights, all conductor elevations, and required clearance envelopes (minimum 7.5 feet horizontal sky-to-ground clearance) are not provided. Please provide detailed electrical profile/section views showing all existing overhead facilities with heights and clearance demonstrations.

applicableAreas: Throughout site, all buildings 1-8
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed transformers (4 pad-mounted), meters (attached to 7 buildings), pull boxes, and underground conduit routing in blue. However, vision analysis identified critical absences: No conduit sizing or material specifications are labeled, no transformer kVA ratings or voltage configurations are shown, no pull box dimensions, no distribution line sizes. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only one transformer pad labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' and lacks all underground routing and meters. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows no electric distribution lines at all. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) has legend symbols for 'Proposed Underground Electric' and 'Transformer Pad' but NO actual facilities are drawn on the plan view.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(iii) and (5) require proposed electric facilities to be 'shown' with sufficient detail. While Sheet 21 provides some proposed facilities (transformers, meters, routing), the incompleteness includes: (1) no conduit/wire sizing, (2) no transformer ratings, (3) no voltage designations, (4) no equipment specifications. More critically, cross-sheet inconsistency means critical sheets (9, 11, 19) do not show the complete proposed design shown on Sheet 21, violating the requirement that proposed facilities be shown across applicable plan sheets. The lack of specifications on Sheet 21 and absence on other sheets together constitute incomplete documentation per UCM § 1.16.0(5).
findings.comment: Proposed electrical facilities are incompletely shown. Please provide: (1) conduit sizing and material specifications for all underground routing on Sheets 9, 11, 19, and 21; (2) transformer pad kVA ratings and voltage configurations; (3) distribution line sizes; (4) pull box dimensions; (5) consistent depiction of all proposed equipment across all plan sheets (Site Plan, Grading, Utility Tap, and Electrical Plan sheets).

applicableAreas: All 8 proposed buildings
findings.observation: Examined electrical design plan and site plan for power source indication. Sheet 21 shows 4 proposed transformer pads and meters on buildings but does not identify which transformer(s) serve which buildings. No callouts or connection lines indicate power routing from transformers to specific buildings. No indication of primary vs. secondary service. Sheet 9 shows one transformer pad but no meters and no indication of service routing. The electrical design does not include a one-line diagram, equipment schedule, or notes identifying the power source for the 39 residential units.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires plans to show 'Power source for proposed buildings.' The omission of this information means: (1) it is unclear which transformer(s) power which buildings, (2) there is no indication whether multiple buildings share service or each has individual service (violating potential unified development documentation), (3) load distribution among transformers cannot be verified. This is a fundamental requirement for demonstrating compliance with UCM § 1.3.3 (one point of service, one service voltage per building).
findings.comment: Power source for proposed buildings not clearly identified. Please add: (1) equipment schedule or one-line diagram showing which transformer(s) serve which buildings; (2) service voltage and load data for each building; (3) connection routing from transformers to each building's service entrance; (4) clarification of whether multiple buildings share service or have individual service points.

applicableAreas: All utility profile sheets
findings.observation: Sheet 21 contains notation 'See Sheet 19 for Profile' directing readers to utility profile information. However, vision analysis of Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) revealed NO profile/section views of any utilities—only plan view drawing with tables. Sheet 19 shows water, wastewater, and storm drain linework and callouts but no vertical cross-sections or profiles. Examination of other sheets (Storm Sewer Plan, Biofiltration Pond Profiles) found drainage and pond profiles but no electric utility profiles.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(iv) requires proposed conduit routing to be shown in profile view. The reference on Sheet 21 to Sheet 19 for profile information appears to be a cross-sheet coordination error—Sheet 19 lacks any electrical profiles. Conduit depth of burial, clearance from other utilities, and elevation coordination cannot be verified without profile views showing the underground electric routing in cross-section.
findings.comment: Proposed conduit routing is not shown in profile/section view. Sheet 21 references Sheet 19 for profiles, but Sheet 19 contains no electrical profiles. Please provide detailed utility profile sections showing proposed electric conduit routing with: (1) depth of burial, (2) clearance from other utilities, (3) clearance from existing structures, and (4) elevation coordination with site grading.

applicableAreas: Western site boundary, point of connection to existing AE facilities
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 21 noted: 'There is no explicit Point of Connection (POC) or Primary Service Point label clearly indicating exactly where the proposed blue line network taps into the existing utility provider's network. Blue routing lines originate near the existing OHE lines in the NW corner (near an Electrical Pull Box) and near the existing underground lines on the West edge, implying connection points in these general areas, but a definitive tie-in detail or label is absent.' The plan shows blue conduit lines approaching existing infrastructure but lacks callout, label, or detail showing the specific connection point.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires the 'Point of connection to existing AE facilities' to be shown. This is a fundamental requirement for demonstrating that the proposed design interfaces correctly with Austin Energy's infrastructure. Without an explicit callout showing exactly where the customer-owned facilities connect to the AE system (i.e., the 'point of service' boundary per UCM § 1.3.3), compliance cannot be verified and AE Design cannot approve the design.
findings.comment: Point of connection to existing Austin Energy facilities is not clearly identified on plans. Please add explicit callouts or a detailed connection diagram showing: (1) exact location where proposed electric service connects to existing AE infrastructure; (2) demarcation point between AE-owned and customer-owned facilities; (3) detailed connection at pole/underground main; (4) applicable voltage and amperage at point of service.

applicableAreas: From point of connection through entire service routing to all buildings
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows blue conduit lines routing throughout the site, but the routing path from the point of connection (which itself is not clearly identified per EL-10.14 finding) to the proposed service point(s)/buildings is not clearly labeled or documented. While conduit lines are drawn, there are no notes, annotations, or callouts explaining the routing path, voltage being carried, or service endpoint. No schematic or one-line diagram shows the electrical service path from AE system to each building.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires 'Proposed electrical route from existing AE service to proposed service [to be] shown.' The current plans show conduit routing graphically but lack the documentation needed to understand: (1) which route serves which building, (2) whether service enters from front or rear, (3) intermediate connection points, (4) service voltage and load at each endpoint. This documentation is essential for demonstrating that the routing complies with AE requirements (e.g., 20-foot maximum meter-to-disconnect distance, meter accessibility, etc.).
findings.comment: Proposed electrical service route from existing Austin Energy connection to proposed service points is not clearly documented. Please provide: (1) one-line electrical schematic showing service path from AE connection point to each building's service entrance; (2) annotations on site plan showing service routing with arrows and labels; (3) notes identifying which route serves which building; (4) identification of any intermediate disconnect/metering locations.

applicableAreas: All transformers and service equipment
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 4 proposed transformer pads with labels 'Electrical Transformer Pad' but no voltage designation is provided. The transformers are not labeled as serving primary (distribution voltage, typically 12.47kV in Austin) or secondary (service voltage, typically 120/208V or 240/480V) voltage. No notes indicate whether these are primary service transformers or secondary distribution/step-down units. Vision analysis found: 'The 'Electrical Transformer Pad' labels do not include the kVA rating or voltage configurations of the transformers.'
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.3 specifies that electrical service must be identified with 'one service voltage' and references understanding the service as primary or secondary. The plans must identify whether the shown transformers are AE-owned primary-to-secondary step-down transformers (most typical for residential service) or customer-owned equipment. This distinction is critical for understanding the service point demarcation and compliance with one-service-voltage requirement. Without this identification, it is unclear whether the design meets the UCM § 1.3.3 requirement.
findings.comment: Electrical service is not identified as primary or secondary voltage. Please provide: (1) transformer pad schedules identifying kVA ratings and voltage configurations (primary/secondary); (2) service voltage identification on site plan (e.g., '120/208V, 3-phase, 4-wire secondary'); (3) clarification of whether transformers are Austin Energy-owned (customer side) or customer-owned equipment; (4) one-line diagram showing voltage levels throughout the system.

applicableAreas: Cover sheet, general notes, utility plan sheets
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 1 (Cover) and 3 (General Notes) for Austin Energy Standard Notes per UCM § 1.16.0. Sheet 3 contains 'Electric Notes' (Block 8) and 'Electric Transmission Notes' (Block 20) addressing tree work, easements, and transmission restrictions. However, these are not comprehensive 'AE Standard Notes'—they address only specific topics. Standard notes typically include: AE right to access and maintain facilities, identification of AE vs. customer facilities, standard electrical specifications, meter location requirements, easement maintenance, etc. No block was found containing comprehensive Austin Energy standard note requirements similar to those required by UCM § 1.16.0(8) plat notes.
findings.reasoning: Reviewer Convention for electric infrastructure plans requires inclusion of 'Austin Energy Standard Notes' on plans, which establish baseline AE requirements, rights, and responsibilities. While Sheet 3 contains some electric-related notes, they focus on transmission restrictions and tree work rather than comprehensive standard notes covering the full range of AE facility maintenance, access, meter, and service requirements. The absence of systematic standard notes leaves the plans incomplete per industry and AE Design practice.
findings.comment: Austin Energy Standard Notes are not provided on plans. Please add comprehensive AE Standard Notes addressing: (1) AE right to maintain and access all AE facilities; (2) distinction between AE-owned and customer-owned infrastructure; (3) meter location and accessibility requirements; (4) easement maintenance and tree clearance obligations; (5) underground facility identification and protection; (6) service point identification and disconnect requirements; (7) reference to UCM sections governing service.

applicableAreas: Utility plan, electrical design plan, site plan
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) for a note stating that all electric infrastructure is shown. Sheet 21 contains 'Utility Notes' (Block 6 from guide.md) with contractor directives to verify utilities but no note stating 'All electric infrastructure including existing and proposed is shown on these plans, or exceptions requiring pre-approval are noted.' The plan shows existing OHE, proposed transformers, and proposed routing but does not include a comprehensive statement that the electric design is complete.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) is the comprehensive requirements section for plan documentation. A standard practice and requirement is for plans to include a note certifying that all existing and proposed electric infrastructure is shown, and if anything is omitted or to be designed later (exceptions), those items must be noted with the requirement for AE pre-approval. This note provides AE Design certainty that the applicant has identified all infrastructure and indicates any gaps. Its absence means AE Design cannot verify the design is complete.
findings.comment: Note missing stating all electric infrastructure (existing and proposed) is shown and exceptions require Austin Energy pre-approval. Please add: 'All existing and proposed electric infrastructure is shown on these plans. Any modifications to electric service, additional facilities, or changes to the shown design require pre-approval from Austin Energy Design. Indicate any infrastructure not yet designed or to be determined.'

applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations, meter locations, access paths
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 21 found: 'Electric equipment dimensions or clearance information: None. There are no text callouts providing the physical dimensions of the transformer pads, pull boxes, or meter banks. There are no drafted clearance zones or textual notes defining required working clearances around the electrical equipment.' Examined Sheets 9, 21, 31 for coordination details: No staging area dimensions (20' × 35'), no truck access paths (12' horizontal × 16' vertical clearance), no setback measurements from transformers to buildings, no bollard details, no mountable curb information, no disconnect location callouts, no measurements for horizontal clearance (10 feet minimum on access door side).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) and § 1.3.16 require 'missing measurements for clearances, disconnect location, staging area, mountable curb, bollard, truck access details' to be shown. These details are essential for: (1) AE equipment installation and maintenance access, (2) ensuring landscaping/buildings don't impair access, (3) verifying compliance with PAD clearance requirements (10 ft on access door, 5 ft on sides), (4) providing 35-foot vertical clearance over 20' × 35' staging area. Their absence prevents verification of compliance and AE operability.
findings.comment: Electric site plan lacks required coordination and clearance details. Please provide: (1) 20' × 35' staging area dimensions and 35' vertical clearance in front of each transformer pad; (2) truck access path dimensions (minimum 12' horizontal width, 16' vertical clearance, capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight); (3) clearance measurements around all transformer pads (10' minimum on access door side, 5' minimum on operator sides); (4) disconnect location and distance from transformer; (5) bollard and protective barrier details; (6) mounting curb specifications for transformer access.

applicableAreas: All plan sheets: site, utility, landscape, grading, irrigation, storm, wet utility
findings.observation: Examined all required plan sheets for electric easement depiction. Sheet 21 shows 5' electric easements with recording info on southern boundary. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows electric easements with citations on eastern and southern boundaries. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows electric easements on eastern and southern boundaries. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) has legend entry for electric in legend but vision found NO easements drawn on the plan itself. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does NOT show electric easements—only shows utilities W, SD, and OHE line. Per facts.md, there are TWO 5' electric easements from Mecey Subdivision plat (Vol 73, Pg 76) plus additional easements from Cortez Heights plat (Vol 64, Pg 13).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires existing electric easements to be shown 'on all required plan sheets' (site, utility, landscape, grading, irrigation, storm, wet utility). Current status: Easements shown on Sheets 9, 11, 21 but MISSING on Sheet 19 and Sheet 31. The incomplete depiction across all sheets means coordination cannot be verified—particularly Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) where trees must not conflict with easement access and maintenance. The omission from Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) creates inconsistency in the utility coordination across sheets.
findings.comment: Existing electric easements are not shown on all required plan sheets. Please add electric easement depictions (with recording information and dimensions) to: (1) Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan); (2) Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan); (3) verify depiction on all other applicable sheets (site, grading, irrigation, storm drain, wet utility sheets).

applicableAreas: All sheets with electric easements
findings.observation: Examined electric easement labels on Sheets 9, 11, 21. The 5' electric easements are labeled as '5' Electric Easement Vol. 73, Pg. 76' or '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 883' but have NO designation indicating whether they accommodate aerial (overhead) or non-aerial (underground) facilities. Sheet 21 shows existing overhead lines (OHE) and existing underground lines but the easements are not explicitly designated as 'Aerial' or 'Underground.' Per UCM § 1.10.0, aerial easements require vertical clearance maintenance (7.5 ft horizontal, 15 ft radius); underground easements require subsurface clearance from other utilities. The failure to distinguish prevents verification of correct easement type.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires plans to 'distinguish between aerial electric easements and underground electric easements.' This is not a formatting preference but a regulatory requirement because aerial and underground easements have different clearance, maintenance, and access requirements per UCM §§ 1.10.3 and 1.10.4. Aerial easements accommodate poles, overhead conductors, guys, and require tree-free zones and vertical clearances. Underground easements accommodate conduit, pad-mounted equipment, and require different horizontal clearances. Without designation, it is unclear what uses are permitted within each easement, and AE staff cannot verify the design accommodates the correct infrastructure.
findings.comment: Plans do not distinguish between aerial and underground electric easements. Please designate each electric easement as either 'Aerial Electric Easement' (for overhead facilities: poles, conductors, guys, with required vertical clearances) or 'Underground Electric Easement' (for subsurface facilities: conduit, pad-mounted equipment) on all plan sheets showing easements.

applicableAreas: Site plan, utility plan, landscape plan, grading plan, storm drain plan, wet utility plan
findings.observation: Examined all required plan sheets for electric facility depiction. Sheet 21 shows: existing OHE, existing underground lines, 4 proposed transformer pads, 7 meter locations, pull boxes, underground routing. Sheet 9 shows: existing OHE, one transformer pad, electric easements. Sheet 11 shows: electric easements only, NO electric lines or equipment. Sheet 19 shows: legend symbols for electric but NO actual electric facilities drawn on the plan. Sheet 31 shows: existing OHE on boundary, NO transformers, NO meters, NO underground routing, NO pull boxes. Vision analysis confirmed sheets 11 and 19 lack the complete electric design, and sheet 31 is missing transformers and staging areas shown on Sheet 21.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires comprehensive depiction of electric facilities across all plan sheets so all design disciplines can coordinate. Fragmented depiction creates risk of conflicts (e.g., landscaping in transformer staging areas, grading encroaching on underground routing, irrigation lines crossing conduit).
findings.comment: Electric facilities are not shown on all required plan sheets. The detailed design on Sheet 21 (transformers, meters, routing) must be repeated on: (1) Sheet 9 (Site Plan); (2) Sheet 11 (Grading Plan); (3) Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan); (4) Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan); (5) all other applicable utility, irrigation, and storm drain sheets. Ensure consistency in facility locations and equipment symbols across all sheets.

applicableAreas: All sheets showing electric equipment
findings.observation: Examined equipment symbols across sheets. Sheet 21 uses: large blue rectangles with zig-zag symbols for transformers labeled 'Electrical Transformer Pad'; small blue circles with 'E' for pull boxes labeled 'Electrical Pull Box'; rectangles on building walls for meters labeled 'Electrical Meters.' Sheet 9 shows one 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' but the symbol and style may differ. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey legend) defines 'TRANSFORMER ON PAD' with a square 'T' symbol. The symbols are not consistent across sheets in terms of graphical representation and labeling style.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires 'Equipment symbols consistent across plan sheets.' This is essential for plan reviewers and contractors to identify equipment reliably across all sheets. Inconsistent symbols create confusion and increase risk of misidentification (e.g., meter vs. disconnect, transformer vs. telecom box). All equipment of the same type must use identical symbols and labels across all sheets.
findings.comment: Equipment symbols are inconsistent across plan sheets. Please establish a consistent legend for all electrical equipment (transformer pads, meters, pull boxes, disconnects) and apply identical symbols and labels on all plan sheets. Include the legend on each sheet showing electric facilities.

applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations, meter locations, pull box locations
findings.observation: Compared facility locations across sheets. Sheet 21 shows 4 transformer pads at specific locations (NW, SW, central-south, central-east). Sheet 9 shows one transformer labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' on the western side, which may correspond to one of the four on Sheet 21 but location does not clearly match. Sheet 31 (Landscape) shows OHE but NO transformer pads, meaning the transformers shown in detail on Sheet 21 are not depicted on the landscape plan. This prevents landscaping coordination with transformer locations.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires 'Electric facility locations do not match across plan sheets' to be avoided. When the same facility (e.g., a transformer pad) is shown on multiple sheets, it must be in the same location relative to buildings, property lines, and other features. Discrepancies or omissions across sheets create confusion about the actual design and prevent verification of proper coordination (e.g., are trees within transformer access zones? is landscaping in staging areas?).
findings.comment: Electric facility locations do not consistently match across plan sheets. Please verify and ensure: (1) all transformer pads shown on Sheet 21 are also shown on Sheets 9, 11, 19, 31 at identical locations; (2) all meters shown on Sheet 21 are also shown on Sheets 9, 31 (landscape elevation); (3) pull boxes and conduit routing shown on Sheet 21 are shown on Sheets 9, 11, 19; (4) use consistent coordinate/dimension references to verify locations match across sheets.

applicableAreas: Transformer pad staging areas, overhead line clearance zones, underground conduit areas
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows trees planted near the OHE line on the southern boundary but vision analysis found: 'There are no specific callouts, notes, or legend entries on this sheet indicating that these specific trees are utility-compatible, low-growing species chosen to coordinate with the overhead lines above them.' No trees are shown in the 20' × 35' staging areas in front of the transformer pads (in fact, the transformer pads themselves are not shown on Sheet 31). Sheet 30 (Existing Tree Plan) does not address coordination with electric infrastructure. There are no notes on any sheet requiring trees within utility clearance zones to be utility-compatible species.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires coordination across sheets, and § 1.10.3 specifies clearance requirements (15-foot radius from primary/neutral conductors, 7.5 feet horizontal minimum clearance). When trees are planted near electric facilities, the landscape plan must show: (1) tree species are chosen to not exceed mature height of 15 feet (typical for utility clearance), (2) trees are not planted within 10-foot radius of transformer access doors (part of 20' × 35' staging area), (3) trees do not interfere with overhead clearance envelopes. The current landscape plan shows trees near OHE without utility-compatibility restrictions, violating coordination requirements.
findings.comment: Tree locations and electric infrastructure locations are not coordinated across plan sheets. Please provide: (1) notes on landscape plan specifying that trees within 15 feet of overhead electric conductors must be utility-compatible species (mature height not exceeding 15 feet); (2) exclusion of all landscaping (trees, shrubs, irrigation) from the 20' × 35' staging area in front of each transformer pad; (3) clearance notes showing trees will not encroach on 7.5-foot horizontal clearance from overhead primary and neutral conductors; (4) cross-reference between landscape plan tree locations and electrical plan transformer/line locations.

applicableAreas: Areas adjacent to transformer pad locations
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 4 transformer pads at specific locations. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does NOT show these transformer pads. Vision analysis confirmed: 'Because the electric transformers and their associated required clearance/staging zones are not drawn on this sheet, it is impossible to determine from this document alone if landscaping elements conflict with those specific staging areas.' Cannot verify whether landscaping (trees, shrubs, hardscape, irrigation) is placed within the required 20' × 35' clear zone with 35' vertical clearance in front of transformer access doors.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 specifies that pad-mounted transformers require 'Minimum 20 feet × 35 feet horizontal clear zone with 35 feet vertical clearance in front of pad-mounted transformers, vaults, and other AE equipment requiring crane/bucket truck access for installation and maintenance.' The landscape plan must show these clearance zones and must not include landscaping within them. Since Sheet 31 does not show the transformer pads, coordination cannot be verified. Without explicit depiction of staging areas and exclusion of landscaping, compliance cannot be determined.
findings.comment: Landscape plans do not demonstrate that landscaping avoids required staging areas adjacent to transformer locations. Please: (1) show all transformer pad locations and their 20' × 35' staging areas (with 35' vertical clearance) on the landscape plan; (2) add note stating no landscaping (trees, shrubs, hardscape) is permitted within these clear zones; (3) provide detail showing how existing landscaping plan respects transformer access requirements.

applicableAreas: Truck access paths to all electric facilities, transformer staging areas
findings.observation: Examined all sheets for truck access path documentation. No sheet shows: (1) identified truck access lanes with 12-foot horizontal width and 16-foot vertical clearance, (2) pavement or surface capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight, (3) unobstructed paths from public right-of-way to transformer pads and other AE equipment, (4) grade changes or barriers that might block access. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) could show access paths but does not. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows grades but does not call out required access surface specifications. Vision analysis found these elements missing from all sheets.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(4) requires plans to 'demonstrate that development preserves AE personnel access to maintain current and proposed facilities.' This requires showing truck access paths that meet AE specifications: (1) 12-foot minimum horizontal width, (2) 16-foot minimum vertical clearance, (3) surface capable of supporting 72,180 lbs. A bucket truck or crane must be able to reach all transformers and disconnect points for installation, maintenance, and emergency repairs. The failure to show and specify access paths prevents verification that AE operability is preserved.
findings.comment: Plans do not demonstrate preserved Austin Energy personnel access to electric facilities. Please provide: (1) truck access paths (12-foot horizontal width minimum, 16-foot vertical clearance minimum) clearly marked on site plan, landscape plan, and grading plan from public right-of-way to each transformer pad and major disconnect location; (2) specification that access surfaces support minimum 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight; (3) grading and landscaping notes confirming no obstructions to access paths; (4) confirmation that grade changes and retaining walls do not block access to facilities.

applicableAreas: All buildings, electrical design documentation
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) for projected load documentation. The sheet shows transformer pads and meters but does not include: (1) kVA ratings for the transformers, (2) amperage capacity of service, (3) load calculations for the 39-unit residential project, (4) notes indicating projected electrical load, (5) equipment schedules with load data. No load analysis or calculations are shown on the electrical plan.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires 'Projected electrical load required for electric service [to be] shown on plans.' This information is critical for AE Design to verify: (1) transformer size is adequate for the load, (2) service amperage is appropriate, (3) no load-related issues exist. Without this documentation, AE Design cannot verify the design is code-compliant and adequate to serve the 39 units.
findings.comment: Projected electrical load for proposed service is not shown on plans. Please provide: (1) load calculation for the 39-unit residential development (in watts or kVA); (2) transformer kVA ratings on all transformer pads; (3) service panel amperage (e.g., 200A, 400A, 600A per building); (4) one-line electrical diagram showing load distribution; (5) verification that transformer size is adequate for projected demand.

applicableAreas: Meter locations on all buildings
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows meters attached to building walls but does not provide documentation regarding: (1) flood elevation verification (meters must be minimum 1 foot above 100-year flood level per UCM § 1.9.3.1), (2) clearance to gas meters (3-foot minimum per UCM § 1.9.3.1(C)(3)), (3) clearance to porches/stairways/overhangs >72 inches, (4) meter accessibility and location on first floor/ground level. Sheet 9 does not show meters at all. Facts.md indicates site is in FEMA Zone X (outside 100-year floodplain), but architectural elevations showing meter locations relative to buildings are not provided in the available documentation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 specifies meter location requirements: (1) outdoors, readily accessible, on first floor/ground level, within sight of transformer; (2) not on/under porches or stairways; (3) not under overhangs >72 inches; (4) minimum 1 foot above 100-year flood elevation; (5) minimum 3-foot separation from gas meters/regulators/relief valves. The plans show meters but do not verify compliance with these location restrictions. Without architectural elevations or detailed meter location callouts showing compliance, UCM § 1.9.3.1 compliance cannot be verified.
findings.comment: Meter location compliance with prohibited locations and flood elevation requirements is not demonstrated. Please provide: (1) architectural elevations showing meter locations relative to building porch/stairway/overhang obstructions; (2) 3-foot separation verification from gas meters (show gas meter locations if present); (3) elevation certificates or grading plan showing meters are minimum 1 foot above 100-year flood level (or FEMA determination if in floodplain); (4) notes confirming meters are readily accessible and on first floor/ground level within sight of transformer.
